Subject: Access controls and support access — follow-up from today's call

Hi Alex / Dana —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our conversation and a few next steps so we stay aligned.

Call recap (high level):
- FinTrust is evaluating Redwood for inference across a mix of hosted + dedicated deployments; primary concerns were around PII handling, data residency, and operational access.
- Security asked for details on access controls (RBAC, least-privilege model), support access patterns (how we enable remote support, break-glass), and auditing (what logs and retention look like).

Answers / next notes:
- RBAC: Redwood supports org/team/project-level roles plus custom roles. You can scope permissions to model, route, and dataset. We also support role inheritance and API-key-scoped rights for service accounts.
- Least privilege: default roles follow least-privilege principles; customers can create role templates (read-only for models, admin for deployment) and assign at the project level.
- Support access / break-glass: support access is off by default. When enabled, we use time-limited access tokens, require a justification and an approval flow, and all sessions are audited. Break-glass requests produce an immutable audit trail and trigger alerts to your security admin.
- Auditing/logs: request/response metadata, admin events, and access sessions are logged. Default retention is 365 days; retention windows can be configured to shorter/longer per contract. Event exports (S3) and SIEM integrations are available.
- Data residency / retention: Data at rest is stored in the region you select; for hosted mode we provide EU and US regions. Retention policies can be configured per-project; we also support purge-on-request workflows.

Attachments included: redwood_access_controls_overview.pdf (RBAC + support access details), SOC2-collection-request.xlsx (security artifacts checklist), mutual_action_plan.docx (proposed next steps & timeline).

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the security contacts you'd like on the next call (security + infra).
2) We can schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with our infra/sec lead — propose Tue 21 Sep 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 22 Sep 13:00-14:00 PT.
3) I will send a draft mutual action plan and the SOC2 artifacts checklist for your team to review.
4) Rishi (cc'ed) will follow up on pricing for Dedicated capacity once we align on scale.

If helpful I can also share a short screencast of the RBAC console and how break-glass approvals look in the audit log.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and for sending the attachments. A couple follow-ups from our security team:

1) Role granularity: Can roles be applied at the model instance level (we need to limit access for certain models that handle more sensitive PII) or is it only project-level? Also, are there managed role templates for common patterns (e.g., data-scientist, infra-ops, support-readonly)?

2) Break-glass: You mentioned dual-approval for break-glass — can you confirm who approves (customer security admin + Redwood on-call?) and whether those approval actions are recorded in the same audit trail. Is there an SLA for responding to break-glass requests if urgent?

3) Auditing: Do logs include the full request/response payloads or only metadata? We have strict controls around storing PII in logs; if payloads are stored we need to understand redaction options and whether logs can be configured to avoid storing inputs/outputs.

4) SOC2 artifacts: we'll need the SOC2 coverage statement and the latest auditor letter; the checklist you sent is helpful — can you point to the specific evidence for privileged access controls and incident response?

Finally, can you provide a ballpark (order-of-magnitude) monthly cost for a Dedicated pool sized for ~200 concurrent inference sessions (mixed sequence lengths)? Procurement (Dana) is cc'ed and will coordinate on contracting.

Appreciate it — once we have the details I'll coordinate internally and confirm attendees for the technical deep-dive.

Alex — thanks for the great questions. Answers below and a few clarifications: 

1) Role granularity: Roles can be scoped at org/team/project AND model levels. You can create custom roles and bind them to individual model endpoints. We also provide out-of-the-box role templates (data-scientist, infra-ops, support-readonly, billing-only) that you can clone and adapt.

2) Break-glass approvals: Break-glass requires a customer-designated security approver AND a Redwood operations approver for initial activation. Approval actions (who approved, timestamp, justification) are recorded in the audit trail. For emergencies we also provide a documented emergency access process with push-notification and 15-minute acknowledgement SLA from on-call (subject to SLA in contract).

3) Auditing / logs: By default we log request/response metadata and admin events. Full payloads are NOT stored in logs unless explicitly enabled; we support payload redaction at the ingestion layer (strip inputs/outputs from logs) and can configure export pipelines that omit payload fields.

4) SOC2 evidence: In the SOC2 collection workbook I highlighted the relevant artifacts for privileged access and incident response (Control IDs A-3, A-7 in the sheet). The SOC2 auditor letter and coverage statement are included in the SOC2 bundle we can share under an NDA — I'll have our compliance lead surface that on the next message.

Pricing: Rishi will follow up with an order-of-magnitude for a Dedicated pool sized for ~200 concurrent sessions — rough estimate will depend on model family & quantization; ballpark today would be in the mid/high four-figures USD per hour for reserved nodes, with monthly commitment options. We'll provide a more concrete SKU-based estimate after we confirm model mix.

Next steps (concrete):
- I'll share a draft mutual action plan (attached) that maps security review, demo, and procurement milestones.
- Please confirm who from FinTrust should be on the technical deep-dive; we recommend security + infra + one product stakeholder.
- Proposed slots again: Tue 21 Sep 10:00 PT / Wed 22 Sep 13:00 PT.

If it's useful I can also set up temporary sandbox access with RBAC restricted to a non-sensitive test model so your team can exercise the break-glass flow and audit logs without touching production data.

Thanks —
